title: Force on moving charges; Alternating current and transformers
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG08-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG08-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG08-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MG03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG03-1#N.3b, MG08-1#N.4, MG03-1#N.6a, MG08-1#N.7, MG03-1#N.17, MG08-1#N.9, MG08-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Frequency
items.clue: Number of cycles each second: 50 Hz for UK mains.

items.label: Peak value
items.clue: Height of an a.c. trace from its centre line to a crest.

items.label: Y-gain
items.clue: Oscilloscope setting giving the volts represented by each division.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Quantity of a moving charge that a magnetic push leaves unchanged, like its speed.

questions.stem: An electron moves towards the right of the page, in the plane of the page, through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the electron at that instant?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the bottom of the page
Towards the left of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.stem: An alternating pd is displayed with the time-base set to 2.0 ms per division. Exactly three complete cycles span 6.0 divisions. What is the frequency of the pd?

A proton moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to its velocity. A second proton moves at twice the speed of the first, perpendicular to the same field. Compared with the first proton, what are the radius of the second proton's circle and the time it takes to complete one revolution?

options.text: Radius halved; time for one revolution reduced to a quarter
Radius doubled; time for one revolution unchanged
Radius unchanged; time for one revolution halved
Radius doubled; time for one revolution halved as well

questions.stem: An alternating supply with a peak pd of 10 V is connected across a 20 Ω resistor. What is the mean power dissipated in the resistor?

Two protons enter two separate regions at the same speed. Region 1 contains only a uniform electric field; region 2 contains only a uniform magnetic field. Each proton enters at right angles to the field lines. Gravity is negligible. A short time later, which statement is correct?

options.text: Both protons still have their starting speed, because each force began at right angles to the motion.
Only the proton in the magnetic field still has its starting speed.
Only the proton in the electric field still has its starting speed.
Both protons have sped up, because each one is pushed by a force.

questions.stem: An alternating pd is displayed with the Y-gain set to 0.50 V per division. The trace measures 6.4 divisions from crest to trough. What is the peak pd?

A signal generator gives a sine wave of peak pd 1.5 V and frequency 500 Hz. It is displayed with the Y-gain at 0.50 V per division and the time-base at 0.50 ms per division. How tall is the trace from crest to trough, and how wide is one cycle?
questions.explanation: Right. Crest to trough = 3.0 V ÷ 0.50 V per division = 6.0 divisions. T = 1/500 = 2.0 ms ÷ 0.50 ms per division = 4.0 divisions.
